label: synth_vc_pinterest_style_memo
draft:
Pinterest is a visual discovery and bookmarking platform that lets users organise images they find interesting onto themed boards. We believe it is a particularly differentiated consumer product, and we recommend a USD 10mm Series A investment at a pre-money valuation of USD 40mm.

What attracted us was the user engagement profile. Average session length on Pinterest is approximately 14 minutes, which compares to roughly 7 minutes on Facebook and 2 to 3 minutes on most social bookmarking products. Users return roughly six times per week on average, and 68% remain active 30 days after first signup. The median active user pins around eight items per week. These are exceptional engagement metrics for a consumer product at this stage.

Pinterest's user base is unusual in two respects. First, 82% of active users are women, an unusually high concentration. Second, the user base skews older than typical social products, with the heaviest concentration in the 25 to 44 age range. This combination — engaged users, female-skewed, older demographic — represents a strong and underserved advertising audience and supports a credible long-term monetisation path through native advertising in categories like home decor, fashion, and weddings.

The founders, Ben Silbermann and Evan Sharp, are first-time founders but our diligence has been deeply positive. Ben in particular has built a reputation at Google for being unusually focused on users and product. Pinterest currently has 8 employees, including the founders, and 1.5 million monthly active users. There is no revenue yet; the founders have deliberately deferred monetisation in favour of growing engagement.

The risks are clear. The product has no monetisation strategy yet. The current engagement profile may not survive scaling beyond the early adopter cohort. Defensibility against well-funded competitive responses is uncertain. We have stress-tested for total loss and consider this an acceptable bet given the conviction we have in the engagement signal and the founders.
